**[t1] Rachel (facilitator):** Welcome Mr. Davis and Dr. Chen. What makes creating the master schedule for the high school so challenging each year?

**[t2] Mr. Davis (stakeholder):** We have twelve hundred students, eighty instructors, and limited specialized science labs. The scheduling system must allocate student course enrollments without room collisions or teacher double-bookings.

**[t3] Rachel (facilitator):** What is the primary constraint regarding faculty teaching load?

**[t4] Dr. Chen (stakeholder):** Full-time teaching staff should not exceed five instructional periods per day to ensure sufficient grading and lesson preparation time.

**[t5] Rachel (facilitator):** How do you schedule specialized facilities like chemistry and biology laboratories?

**[t6] Mr. Davis (stakeholder):** Lab courses require dedicated wet-bench access. We need to assign specialized science laboratory spaces based on wet-lab equipment requirements.

**[t7] Rachel (facilitator):** Should science laboratories be blocked into single periods or double periods?

**[t8] Mr. Davis (stakeholder):** Advanced biology and chemistry laboratories must always be scheduled in consecutive double periods on the same day so experiments finish properly.

**[t9] Rachel (facilitator):** Dr. Chen, does that block scheduling work from the academic curriculum perspective?

**[t10] Dr. Chen (stakeholder):** Consecutive double periods destroy split-period humanities scheduling across elective blocks, so lab periods must remain split across alternate days.

**[t11] Rachel (facilitator):** We have an open contradiction between consecutive double blocks and split-period distribution. What about teacher room movements?

**[t12] Dr. Chen (stakeholder):** The timetable must never schedule junior teachers to more than three distinct classroom relocations in a single instructional day, because carting teaching materials across campus exhausts them.

**[t13] Rachel (facilitator):** That is an important teacher welfare anti-goal. How do you accommodate student elective preferences?

**[t14] Mr. Davis (stakeholder):** The scheduling algorithm should maximize placement of students into their top-choice elective courses.

**[t15] Rachel (facilitator):** Who else has strong opinions about the bell schedule and lunch periods?

**[t16] Mr. Davis (stakeholder):** The student council representatives have strong views about split lunch shifts, but unfortunately no student union delegates have been consulted yet.

**[t17] Rachel (facilitator):** Could attendance tracking be incorporated directly into the schedule?

**[t18] Rachel (facilitator):** What if the system used facial recognition cameras at classroom doors to automatically verify teacher and student attendance as they enter?

**[t19] Dr. Chen (stakeholder):** No, that is completely invasive and absurd for our school community.

**[t20] Mr. Davis (stakeholder):** I completely agree with Dr. Chen; biometric surveillance has no place in our school.

**[t21] Rachel (facilitator):** What is the ultimate measure of scheduling success?

**[t22] Dr. Chen (stakeholder):** A calm, conflict-free start to the school year where every student and faculty member knows exactly where they belong.
